pairs.difference: A: the cap is one flat black-dark mass with a thin lit edge on the board, sitting on a soft lighter disc; rms 0.165 is at the real limit. B: the boot is dark almost everywhere, with hard streak highlights on the toe, black heel and shaft interior, and a small hot white ring behind the ankle. B's rms 0.174 is above the real range and its gap -0.342 is further out than A's -0.312. A is also out on gap, so this is a weak lean.
pairs.fix: Lift the boot's leather to a mid brown so it is not near-black against the orange. Soften the toe highlight into a broad gradual sheen, keep black only in the boot opening and under the heel, and remove the small bright spot behind the ankle.

pairs.difference: A: the rope is a light hero on a single mid-grey background, chopped into small white and grey twist streaks. There is no real dark group, only the small dark binding, and rms 0.086 sits on the floor of the real range. B: the scarf is a large dark mass on two background values, with one concentrated black pocket inside the collar, which matches where real cards put their darkest accent.
pairs.fix: Give the coil a deep soft shadow between its loops and under it, and let the rope's lower side fall to a darker gold. Keep the highlights broad along the top of each coil instead of on every twist.

pairs.difference: A: the card darkens hard to near-black-green corners (vignette 0.134, above real range) around a brighter glow band that rings the jacket. Inside the hero there are clipped white patches on the sleeves, plus a dark sash. B: the hat sits on broad even rays, with light and mid masses and one black accent under the brim. Its corners darken only moderately.
pairs.fix: Keep the green background at a nearly even brightness out to the corners, with no dark edge and no ring of glow around the jacket. Let the sleeves shade softly without white hot spots.

pairs.difference: A: the anchor is a heavy dark blue shape, almost all one dark level, on a pale yellow card with a bright patch behind the shank and hard black at the lower fluke. rms 0.183 and gap -0.398 are both outside the real range. B: the caravan is a large light cream mass on a mid purple field, with darks only in the windows and under the chassis. All its numbers are in range.
pairs.fix: Paint the anchor in a mid blue with a wide soft sheen across its faces. Keep the darkest blue only for the undersides, and keep the yellow stripes even behind it with no bright patch beside the shank.

pairs.difference: A: the mug has broad value shapes, with a large mid body, two big light reflections and one dark contact shadow, on a graded striped wall. B: the arch has no large internal groups. It breaks into hundreds of small light and dark leaf and petal flecks against clipped white stripes and a white glow inside the arch. Mean 0.749 is at the top of the range, rms 0.169 is at the top, and gap -0.278 is below the real range.
pairs.fix: Group the leaves into a few big darker clusters with soft shading inside each, and keep the roses as simple mid-pink shapes. Tone the background stripes down from white to soft pink, with no bright glow inside the arch.

pairs.difference: A: the computer has a clean clipped-light body, a large black screen and calm background bands, and it is the same card shown as REAL in the lessons. B: the saddle is a mid-dark hero, but the fence breaks into streaky white and grey fragments, and there is a blown patch of bright background under the seat. The light and dark groups are less settled. Numbers are in range, with gap near the real limit at -0.24.
pairs.fix: Paint the fence rails as one even warm mid tone with a soft top light and no streaks. Keep the blue background at one steady brightness behind the saddle.

pairs.difference: A: the saloon doors are mid-dark on a mid background, with a gentle overall key and a soft floor light. B: the sneakers sit on a clipped near-white floor and clipped white soles, so the bottom half of the card is one blown light mass. Mean 0.762 is above the real range and vignette -0.009 is at its floor, while the shoe body is mid-dark with hard black seams.
pairs.fix: Make the floor a warm mid yellow instead of near white, and shade the soles to a soft pale grey-lilac toward the ground. Let the wall and floor darken slightly toward the card edges.

pairs.difference: A: the cart has a full range, with dark corners, a dark red body, black wheels and bright awning stripes, and everything is in range. B: the cactus sits in the same two mid levels as the sand and wall, with no dark accent anywhere. The hero separates by hue, not value, and rms 0.087 is well below the real range of 0.120 to 0.195.
pairs.fix: Add a deep green shadow side down the cactus, a dark contact shadow where it enters the sand, and a darker orange wall behind it, so the green stands apart even in black and white.

pairs.difference: A: the barrel is a mid-dark hero on a lighter glow patch, with its darkest value at the base shadow. B: the chest is a light gold hero on dark blue corners, with black inside the lid. All numbers are in range for both, and each has one clear dark group, so my vector gives no reason to choose.

A: the wagon's cover is one big clipped light mass over a mid-dark timber body and wheels. B: the boat is a mid hero on mid water, with a dark pocket under the hull and fine ripple rings. Both are in range with clear groups, and the differences are subject-driven.

A: the locomotive is a huge near-black mass with hard white pipe and rim highlights and a clipped white headlamp, against a white sky band. rms 0.223 and gap -0.321 are both far outside the real range. B: the coaster has a light and mid hero with dark blue track and broad cloud masses, and it misses by only small amounts (gap -0.217, vignette 0.117).
pairs.fix: Paint the locomotive boiler in a dark charcoal blue rather than black, with soft wide highlights along the curve instead of thin white lines. Dim the headlamp glow and bring the sky behind it down to a soft mid yellow.

pairs.difference: A: the gloves are a mid-dark hero with small hot white spots on smooth rounded leather and black pooled beneath them. The wall is lighter at the corners and darker toward the middle-right, so the vignette is reversed (-0.103, below the real range). B: the snorkel scene has many busier groups, but its corners darken normally and its numbers are in range.
pairs.fix: Light the blue wall so it is brightest behind the gloves and slightly darker at the top corners. Spread the glove highlights into wide soft sheens rather than small white dots.

pattern: Generated cards break value in three main ways. First, they miss the real range at the extremes: a hero pushed near-black against a bright card (p04 anchor, p11 train), or blown clipped-white surfaces (p07 floor and soles). Second, they lose grouping: real cards hold a few large masses, while generated heroes fragment into many small light and dark flecks with hot highlights (p05 arch). Third, they place light and dark artificially: a glow hugging the hero or a forced dark corner (p03), a reversed corner falloff (p12), or hue-only separation with no dark accent at all (p08 cactus). Real cards keep one concentrated dark pocket, usually a contact shadow or interior, and let highlights roll off broadly.
